walkthroughs.body_html:
Slave ships were specially built to carry as many people as possible.

The famous ship Brookes could carry over 450 captives, packed in like cargo. The diagram of the Brookes shocked many British people when abolitionists printed it.

Conditions were filthy. Diseases like dysentery spread fast. Roughly 1 in 7 captives died on the journey. 😢

Most enslaved Africans were taken to Caribbean sugar plantations on islands like Jamaica and Barbados, or to tobacco and cotton fields in the American colonies.

Work was from sunrise to sunset. Overseers used whips to keep enslaved people working. People were treated as property, not as humans.

Families were often split up at slave markets. Children born on plantations were also born enslaved.

Enslaved people resisted in many ways. Some worked slowly or broke tools. Some ran away.

Some, called Maroons, escaped to mountain forests in Jamaica and fought back. There were also major revolts — for example, the great revolt of Saint-Domingue (Haiti) from 1791.

People also kept African songs, religions and stories alive — passing them on for hundreds of years. 🌺
